description: Illustrative sample incident for interface testing. Not a real investigation. Numbers are shaped after the Sep 12 cache proof but every event is marked illustrative.
replayRules: The replay assigns id, incidentId, sequence and occurredAt. It replaces alert_received label, startedAt and deadlineAt with real values (deadlineAt = received + 30 minutes). delayMs is the pause before each event.

events.summary: Recommendation service restarted after running out of memory
Reading logs, memory and deploy history
Memory climbed from 45 MiB to 237 MiB in 25 seconds, then the container restarted

payload.summary: Memory climbed from 45 MiB to 237 MiB in 25 seconds before the restart

events.summary: Docker recorded an out-of-memory kill for recommendation

payload.summary: One oom event followed by die and start
payload.excerpt: oom recommendation; die recommendation exitCode=137; start recommendation

events.summary: Flag recommendationCacheFailure default changed from off to on 12 minutes before the alert

payload.summary: Default variant of recommendationCacheFailure changed from off to on

events.summary: About 1 in 100 recommendation requests failed in the last 5 minutes

payload.summary: Error rate about 1 percent, rising after each restart
payload.excerpt: ListRecommendations errors 1.1%; canary /api/recommendations 500 twice in 5 minutes

events.summary: CPU stayed under 30 percent until the memory spike

payload.summary: CPU normal before the spike, so plain overload is unlikely

events.summary: Brief: recommendations fail after the service runs out of memory

payload.summary: Shoppers get errors on recommendations because the service runs out of memory and restarts. A cache flag was turned on shortly before.

knownFacts.text: The service was killed for using too much memory
Memory climbed quickly before the kill
The cache failure flag was switched on 12 minutes earlier

unknowns: Whether customers can tolerate the current failure rate while a fix is tested
How much traffic it takes to trigger the crash
payload.nextStep: Reproduce the crash in the sandbox copy with the flag on

events.summary: Hypothesis: the cache failure flag makes memory grow with each request

payload.claim: With recommendationCacheFailure on, each request grows the in-memory cache until the 500 MiB limit is hit
payload.predicted: Flag on plus about 100 requests reproduces an out-of-memory kill; flag off does not

events.summary: Hypothesis: a traffic spike overloaded the service

payload.claim: A sudden traffic spike exhausted memory regardless of the flag
payload.predicted: 400 requests with the flag off would also crash the service

events.summary: Question for the operator: is the customer impact tolerable?

payload.text: Recommendations are failing on about 1 in 100 requests. Is that tolerable while I test a fix, or should I rush the safest fix first?
payload.whyItMatters: If it is urgent, I go straight to the safest mitigation and verify it. If it is tolerable, I finish checking the other explanation before choosing.
payload.meanwhile: NightCall keeps reproducing the crash in the sandbox copy.

events.summary: Reproducing the crash in the sandbox copy

payload.assignment: Reproduce the out-of-memory crash with the flag on

events.summary: Checks recorded before any experiment ran
Experiment: flag on, restart, up to 400 requests at 5 per second

payload.purpose: Show the crash happens with the flag on under normal traffic

events.summary: 101 requests sent, memory at 73 MiB
Crash reproduced: out-of-memory kill and a failed request at request 122
Reproduction accepted after independent review

reasons: Original code image and source checksum unchanged
Healthy baseline passed before the fault

events.summary: Operator: rush the safest fix

payload.text: Not tolerable, customers are seeing it. Rush the safest fix first.

events.summary: Cache flag hypothesis supported

payload.reason: Reproduced with the flag on; operator asked for the safest fix first

events.summary: Traffic spike hypothesis contradicted

payload.reason: CPU was normal before the spike and the flag explains the growth

events.summary: Mitigation: turn the cache failure flag off and restart recommendation

payload.explanation: Turning the flag off stops the cache from growing; a restart releases memory already held.
caveats: Recommendations lose the cached results until the cache warms again
payload.notFixed: The cache still has no size limit when the flag is on; this is a mitigation, not a repair
